basis: We chose these values and they may not be ideal; the report re-ranks the languages under random perturbations of all of them and only calls an order stable if it survives. The score of a cell is  reach x product of the factors of its obstacles;  the score of a language is the weighted mean of its cells over the probed features (Absent counts 0). `obstacles` is ordered from least to most damaging, and the order is the reasoned part: it follows what each obstacle takes away from the developer. The factors are the numbers read off that order. rating.md re-ranks the languages with every number perturbed (the order of the obstacles kept) and only calls an ordering robust if it survives.

obstacles.why: A build setting: a flag, config file or linker argument. One line of the build, supported, deterministic, reversible, nothing at run time. The type checker no longer sees the feature, but the toolchain still validates the setting.

One call site depends on something marked experimental or unstable, on a supported compiler. It may change in an update, but the damage is local and the rest of the project builds on the stable release.

The whole project, and every project that depends on it, needs a compiler that is not a supported release and can break from one day to the next. Wider than one call site, but the code is still type-checked and deterministic, and the constraint ends when the feature is stabilised.

The module only runs on certain hosts: it imports WASI functions or JS glue code (C++ exceptions need a WASI host, Kotlin's externref build a JS host). Some deployment targets are lost, but most projects target one kind of host anyway and a wide set remains; the code itself is unaffected.
Every module carries extra code: a runtime shipped inside it (322 KB of libc++abi for C++ exceptions). A permanent size cost paid by every user of the module, but the module still runs anywhere.

The feature is written as hand-written assembly or Wasm text. Deterministic and supported, but there is no language help: the syntax is per target, it is verbose and error-prone to write and to maintain, and unless the language happens to check the block against the program, mistakes surface only at assembly or run time. This is the price of the expression itself, so it is charged whether or not the compiler checks the block; that is recorded separately (`checked`) and does not change the factor.

The module must be built for a different backend and gives up everything only the first backend offers. The features of the two backends are mutually exclusive in one module: using this one removes the others.
